findings.title: Retry cleanup deletes non-SMS workflow reminders
findings.body: The new OR branch matches any WorkflowReminder with retryCount > 1, not just SMS reminders. WorkflowReminder is shared by email, SMS, and WhatsApp, so any non-SMS row that ever reaches retryCount > 1 (including future code paths that use this shared column) will be deleted by this cron. The branch also ignores the scheduled state, so a scheduled row with retryCount > 1 would be deleted while its external scheduled job still exists. Scope the condition to the intended SMS/failed reminders, for example by including method: WorkflowMethods.SMS and the intended scheduled state.

findings.title: Retry count increment is a lost-update race
findings.body: Both new increments use reminder.retryCount + 1 with the value read before the Twilio call. If two cron executions (or a retried request) process the same reminder concurrently, both can read the same retryCount and write the same incremented value, so a failure is lost. The reminder can then keep retrying past the intended two-failure limit and never be deleted. Use an atomic Prisma increment such as { retryCount: { increment: 1 } } or an equivalent SQL update.

findings.title: Catch increments retries even when the SMS was already scheduled
findings.body: The try block includes the prisma.workflowReminder.update at lines 169-177 that records a successful Twilio send. If twilio.scheduleSMS succeeds but that database update throws, the catch block increments retryCount and leaves scheduled false. The next cron run sends the same SMS again, and the new delete logic can eventually remove the row, losing the referenceId of the already-scheduled Twilio message so it cannot be cancelled. Retry increments should only happen for actual twilio.scheduleSMS failures; persistence errors after a successful send need separate handling.

findings.title: Missing sendTo or empty message never increments retryCount
findings.body: If sendTo is missing or message is empty, this condition is false and the loop continues without calling Twilio and without throwing. No retryCount increment occurs, so the reminder remains unscheduled and is picked up again on every cron run forever, which is exactly the infinite-retry behavior this PR is trying to stop. Handle this skip case by incrementing the retry counter, deleting the invalid reminder, or otherwise recording the failure.

findings.title: No index for the retryCount cleanup query
findings.body: The cron now runs deleteMany with a predicate on retryCount > 1, but the migration adds no index for retryCount. On a large WorkflowReminder table this OR predicate can force a full scan on every cron invocation, even though almost all rows have retryCount 0. Add an appropriate index (for example a partial index on retryCount > 0, or a composite index with method) to keep the cleanup query efficient.

findings.title: No tests for the destructive retry cleanup path
findings.body: The PR adds retry accounting and a deleteMany that permanently removes workflow reminder rows, but no test covers the new behavior. Add tests for: SMS scheduling failure incrementing retryCount, success after a retry, deletion at the retry threshold, non-SMS reminders not being deleted, and concurrent increments not losing failures.
